html:
American writer and speaker who escaped slavery and became the leading voice of the movement to abolish it. Born enslaved in Maryland, he secretly learned to read. In 1838 he escaped to the North disguised as a sailor.

Abolitionists led by William Lloyd Garrison soon hired him as a lecturer. His life story, the Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass (1845), was a bestseller. It also put him in danger of recapture, so he toured Britain and Ireland, where friends bought his freedom.

Back home he started his own newspaper, The North Star. He spoke for women's right to vote at the Seneca Falls Convention of 1848. His speech "What to the Slave Is the Fourth of July?" (1852) is still read every year.

In the Civil War he met Abraham Lincoln and recruited Black soldiers for the Union. Later he held federal posts, including minister to Haiti. He was the most photographed American of his century, which he used to show Black dignity.
